subject: Human Evolution
title: Homo Erectus: The Committed Walker
description: A short lesson to help you apply Homo Erectus: The Committed Walker.

hook.text: By 1.8 million years ago, Homo erectus had a body almost indistinguishable from ours below the neck.

buildup.text: Long legs, short arms, a narrow pelvis, and arched feet—fully committed to ground-based locomotion.

discovery.text: Turkana Boy's skeleton shows proportions built for long-distance walking in hot, open environments.

twist.text: With these proportions, Homo erectus could cover larger ranges than any earlier hominin species.

climax.text: This body plan was so successful it persisted for over a million years with minimal change.

punchline.text: Nature found a design and stuck with it.

quiz.question: What made Homo erectus a 'committed walker'?
options: Modern body proportions: long legs, short arms
